tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

chen19-device-wafer: Section 2, p.1: the paper states its own wafer (X-cut Mg-doped LNOI, 500 nm film, 2 um oxide, Si).
chen19-mg-doping-purpose: Section 2, p.1: the authors state why they chose Mg-doped film for their own device; a design choice, stated as such.
chen19-fab-process: Section 2, p.1: poling by the process of [5], then EBL racetrack definition, then standard ion milling [6,7]; the paper states its own steps.
chen19-geometry: Figure 1(a) caption, p.2: top width 1.8 um, straight length 300 um, half-ring radius 120 um, poling in one straight section.
chen19-design-mode-d33: Section 2, p.1: for X-cut they use TE00 modes to access d33 (~27 pm/V); the paper states its own mode choice.
chen19-double-resonance-requirement: Section 2, p.1: the authors state the phase matching condition of their racetrack (QPM plus double resonance) and their temperature tuning method.
chen19-pump-and-coupling-setup: Section 2, p.1: Santec 550 laser, polarization controller, 2 um tapered fibers with 5 dB and 6 dB per facet losses; the paper states its own measurement setup.
tunability-gap-unmodeled-effects: Section 2, p.4: measured 1.71 nm/K vs simulated 0.6 nm/K; the authors state thermal expansion and pyroelectric effects are not in the model and are left to future work. The value does not claim they explain the gap.
measurement-setup: Section 2, p.3 and Fig. 4 caption: 1-mm PPLN, CW Santec laser, quasi-TM mode, 2 um tapered fibers, power meter, T = 45 C.
fabrication-wafer-and-etch: Section 1.B, p.2: Z-cut LNOI, 700 nm film on 2 um oxide, ~480 nm ion-mill etch, 2 um PECVD oxide overclad.
fabrication-poling-conditions: Section 1.B, p.2: 30 nm Cr and 60 nm Au electrodes, several 1 ms ~550 V pulses, ~300 C heater; the "critical factor" remark is the authors own stated process note.
sim-setup-two-waveguides: Section 1.A, p.2 and Fig. 1 caption: Lumerical MODE with temperature-dependent Sellmeier, the two geometries, 62 deg sidewall, periods 2.45 um and 3.8 um.
microring-and-wafer-geometry: Section 2, p.3: Z-cut LNOI, 700 nm film on 2 um oxide on Si; ring top width 1.75 um, radius 80 um.
etch-pulley-poling-parameters: Section 2, p.3: 410 nm etch, 290 nm remaining, ~67 deg; pulley 400 nm, 650 nm gap, 80 um; period 4.0 um, 1 ms 525 V pulses.
modulator-electrode-geometry: Section 2, p.3-4: 30 nm Cr and 300 nm Au GSG electrode, 1.5 um waveguide, 5/50 um pads, 3 um gap, 0.14 cm effective length; the pad-width trade-off is the authors stated design rationale.
fig3d-comparison-scope: Figure 3 caption, p.6: Fig. 3(d) includes only milliwatt or sub-milliwatt results; the two excluded demonstrations are named.
locking-actuator-and-power-stabilization: Section 3.3, p.8: amplitude modulation port (400 kHz), pump held within +-0.2 dB by a fixed-output EDFA.
limitations-and-future-feedback-loops: Section 3.3, p.8: the authors attribute the 48 to 41 percent drop to coupling drift and state this as a limit of the current lock, with future remedies.
manual-engagement-of-lock: Section 3.3, p.8: the lock is engaged manually near resonance; the paper states its own procedure.
rabi-angle-definition: Main text p.5: the internal Rabi rotation angle is defined as theta = 2 g Q_p,i / omega_p, with its interpretation given.
device-geometry: Device design, p.3: radius 80 um, 600 nm height, 1700 nm top width.
wavelength-bands-and-modes: Device design and characterization, pp.3-4: C-band pump and signal, visible SF; modes 1560.15, 1551.85, 778.00 nm; m_p=602, m_s=606, m_f=1357, M=149.
mode-and-polarization: Device design, p.3: all waves in fundamental quasi-TM modes using d33 with over 90 percent overlap.
poling-parameters: Methods, p.7: period 3.37 um from 2 pi R / M with M=149, near 50 percent duty cycle, several 1 ms 450 V pulses.
wafer-and-etch: Methods, p.7: Mg-doped Z-cut LNOI, 600 nm film on 2 um oxide, 430 nm etched leaving 170 nm, ~64 deg sidewall.
pulley-coupler-dimensions: Methods, p.7: pulley top width 400 nm, gap 650 nm, length 40 um, aimed at overcoupling both bands.
qe-definition: Device design, p.3, Eq. (3): eta_QE = N_f / N_s with N_s and N_f defined at the cavity input and output.
hamiltonian-definition: Device design, Eq. (1): the effective Hamiltonian and the meaning of g are stated in the paper.
qpm-condition-definition: Device design, Eq. (2): the paper states what the delta function and the orders m_j and M denote.
pump-mode-choice-raman: Device characterization, p.3: the authors state they designate the 1560.15 nm mode as pump to reduce Raman background; a stated design choice.
operating-conditions: Low-noise frequency conversion, p.4: signal fixed ~37 nW on chip, pump raised, temperature 45 +-0.3 C and wavelengths +-20 pm tuned.
temperature-tuning: Device design, p.3: ~0.01 C fine temperature tuning for triple resonance.
noise-measurement-setup: Low-noise frequency conversion, p.4: pump-only noise through free-space filters on a Si SPD, 50 percent efficiency, 250 Hz dark count.
detection-efficiency-17: p.5: total detection efficiency ~17 percent = 50 percent x 33.5 percent; filters removed and lensed fiber per Supplement B.
fig4-corrections: Fig. 4 caption, p.5: 250 Hz dark counts subtracted, 4.75 dB coupling loss and 50 percent detector efficiency accounted for.
snspd-monitoring: Supplement B, p.2: ID281 SNSPDs (85 percent, 100 Hz) monitor input flux with ~50 dB attenuation per channel for a ~20 MHz saturation rate.
coupled-mode-assumptions: Supplement A, p.1: the equations neglect Rayleigh backscattering and assume the single-mode condition; solved with a split-step method.
table-s1-dissipation-rates: Table S1, Supplement p.2: the simulation input rates are listed as given.
table-1-scope-over-10: Table I caption, p.2: the table includes only works with efficiency over 10 percent.
further-work-limit: Introduction, p.2: the authors state a good journey remains and that cavity quality must improve for strong photon-photon interaction.
pulley-visible-ir-overcoupling: Methods, p.7: the pulley coupler is made to give overcoupling for both visible and infrared light; a stated design goal.
scope-no-full-paradigm: Section 2, p.3: the paper states it does not propose a full paradigm, studies the encoding only, and does not fully describe entropy computing.
scope-photon-loss-ignored: Section 2, p.3: photon loss is ignored throughout and may have a major effect; the goal is mathematical, not a full experimental paradigm.
def-dipne: Section 1, p.2: "We call this scheme Differential Photon Number Encoding (DiPNE)" with the encoding defined; DiDE named alongside.
def-dide: Section 3, p.6 and Fig. 1 caption: DiDE is defined as encoding into relative displacement, measured by homodyne; DiPNE uses photon number.
kitten-state-definition-and-preparation: Section 5.1, p.11: "A kitten state is a quadrature squeeze vacuum with photons subtracted", with the in-principle preparation scheme described.
kitten-probabilistic-preparation: Fig. 5 caption, p.10: the authors state the preparation is only probabilistic.
def-squeezed-cat-state: Section 5.1, Eq. 28, p.13: the generalised cat-like target state is defined and the fitting procedure (fixed total photons, optimised squeezing fraction) is stated. The fidelity results are not in the value.
open-question-single-photon-curve: Section 5.1, p.13: the authors state they do not know the origin of the difference and leave it to future work.
hom-generalization-odd-inputs: Section 5.2, p.15-16: the odd-odd result is stated and proved by the binomial term counting of Eqs. 30-34, with the equal-output amplitude shown to cancel termwise; the corollary for odd superpositions follows directly. The equations are garbled in the text layer but the argument is in the paper.
chukwu-2026-numerical-methods-setup: Section 6, p.18-19 and Data availability: Python with numpy, scipy, matplotlib, Jupyter; truncated state space with levels in the captions; analytic initialisation of squeezed states; public code and data stated.
figure-truncation-levels: Fig. 6, 7, 8 and 10 captions: truncation of 1000, 1500 and 100 photons per mode as stated in the captions.
appendixA-displacement-separates: Appendix A, Eqs. 36-48, p.19-20: for a two-mode state with zero mean displacement the output photon number splits into a displacement part and a structure part, derived in the paper. The "well controlled loss" remark is the authors stated expectation and is attributed as such.
appendixA-counterexample-class: Footnote 39, p.27: the authors give an explicit state outside the parity class and say it is unclear how it would arise.
affiliation-and-interest-disclosure: Acknowledgments and Disclosures, p.26: all authors were fully supported by Quantum Computing Inc and hold shares or options there; a disclosed interest, which the paper states about its own work. No better basis fits.

theory_low.theory-gvm-controls-tunability: A first-order Taylor derivation (Eqs. 2-4) that neglects thermal expansion and holds the period fixed. The value drops the thermal-expansion neglect, and the paper itself finds measured tuning about 3 times the model (Section 2, p.4). Equations are garbled in the text layer. Not a theorem the paper states and proves under checked conditions.
theory_low.theory-sign-of-gvm-sets-direction: Rests on a cited thermo-optic inequality [15] and on the authors own statement that GVM is always negative in other LNOI devices; not proved here.
theory_low.sim-tuning-opposite-signs: A simulation outcome (0.2 nm/K red shift, 0.6 nm/K blue shift) from one model; a computed result, and the GVM numbers are extracted from it.
theory_low.thicker-film-positive-small-gvm: A simulation-based design statement and the authors claim; not a proved result.
theory_low.modulator-gsg-vpi-length: Section 3.2, p.7: a COMSOL simulation estimate (~10 V cm) and a stated 1.3 times enhancement; a simulated result, not a measurement or proof.
theory_low.optimal-pump-power: Eq. (5) and the 115 uW figure are an estimate from the authors formula using their own 65 percent and 4.5 percent/uW values; a calculated result, with the formula garbled in the text layer, not a proved result.
theory_low.phase-to-displacement-translation: Section 3, p.4-5: described in prose with the equation garbled; the beamsplitter translation is argued, not stated as a theorem with a proof in the paper.
theory_low.dipne-equals-vacuum-detection: Section 3, p.5: follows from Eq. 6, which is garbled in the text layer, with no formal statement or proof; the condition itself is not in the quotes.
theory_low.dipne-vs-dide-equivalence: Section 3, p.6: a qualitative argument; the "equivalent on average" claim for coherent states and the DiDE preference are stated, not proved.
theory_low.homodyne-gaussian-simulable: Section 3, p.6: a background fact about Gaussian systems (Boson sampling), stated without proof, plus an inference from it.
theory_low.interaction-by-interference-design: Section 4, p.6-7: a conceptual circuit description with the phase symbol garbled; the loss claims are qualitative.
theory_low.interference-loss-formula-coherent: Section 4, Eqs. 9-15, p.7: Eq. 15 is garbled and not in the quotes, so the value cannot be checked from them; the sign statement is an interpretation. Not stated as a numbered result with a proof.
theory_low.loss-independent-of-squeezing: Section 4, p.7: argued from a cited fact about Gaussian states [26]; the non-Gaussian extension is deferred to appendix A and covers a limited class.
theory_low.quantum-erasure-by-strong-coherent-state: Section 4.1, Eqs. 17-18, p.9: a Taylor-expansion argument whose ratio condition is not in the quotes; the physical claim of erasure is the authors interpretation.
theory_low.erasure-condition-and-practicality: Section 4.1, p.9-10: the authors say these are simple calculations and more practical methods are likely; a claim and interpretation, not a proved result.
theory_low.kitten-parity-and-symmetry: Section 5.1, p.11: stated as observations from Eq. 19, which is garbled; the large second-moment claim is not shown; no theorem and proof.
theory_low.kitten-photon-number-peak-estimate: Section 5.1, Eqs. 22-26, p.11-12: the authors call it a crude large-n approximation; the formulas are not in the quotes.
theory_low.photon-number-grows-with-detections: Section 5.1, p.12: a consequence of the authors approximation (Eq. 25), with an intuitive explanation; not proved.
theory_low.kitten-infinite-squeezing-limit: Section 5.1, Eq. 27, p.12: a limit stated with a garbled equation; the convergence is asserted, not proved.
theory_low.arbitrarily-many-photon-kitten: Section 5.1, p.12: "Mathematically speaking" claim in prose, resting on the approximation of Eq. 25, with no proof or check.
theory_low.hom-proof-even-case-nonzero: Section 5.2, p.16: the odd cancellation is proved, but the even case is argued only by an unmatched middle term and a parity count, which does not by itself show a nonzero sum; the paper backs it numerically (Fig. 8). The odd half is covered by hom-generalization-odd-inputs.
theory_low.odd-gives-well-defined-bit: Section 5.2, p.16: a stated consequence for idealised states; the advantage is claimed, not separately shown.
theory_low.gaussian-driving-squeeze: Section 5.3, Eq. 35, p.16-17: an analytic estimate that relies on cited formulas [24,26], with a "conservative estimate" for chosen inputs; the formula is garbled and not in the quotes.
theory_low.squeezing-does-not-disrupt-encoding: Section 5.3, p.17: depends on the earlier independence argument, which is itself an argument, not a proved result for the stated cases.
theory_low.appendixA-parity-class: Appendix A, Eqs. 49-56, p.20-21: the authors say a completely general argument is not possible, the class is limited, and the claims on squeezed vacuum, cat-like and kitten states are asserted; equations garbled.
